steps: Fresh browser context, learner 'Rev P sam6', take a 5-question 1.3 quiz (5 mistakes)
Second fresh browser context, enter exactly the same name, Start
Open Progress and Review mistakes there
checked: The chooser now says 'Progress and mistakes are saved in this browser only, under your name — another browser or device starts fresh. No password.' The second browser shows 'No quizzes yet.' / 'Nothing to review', which is exactly what the new wording promises. Network log for the whole run is still only GET / and GET /app.js, and the profile still lives in localStorage (stats-profile, stats-profile:<id>) — consistent with the claim as now worded.

steps: Learner, section 1.3, 10-question quiz
Answer questions 1-3, click Next so 'Question 4 of 10' shows
Press browser reload
Finish the quiz, open Progress
checked: After reload the page still shows 'Question 4 of 10' with the three earlier answers kept (saved session index 3, three recorded results). Finishing gives 'Section 1.3: 7 / 10 correct' and Progress shows ANSWERED 10 for the 10-question quiz — no double counting. Reloading mid-review also resumes (see D1 below).

steps: Finish a 5-question 1.3 quiz so the results page shows
Press reload
checked: The results page comes back unchanged ('Section 1.3: 3 / 5 correct (60%)', Missed this time, Review mistakes / Retake / Print). The quiz is not restarted.

steps: Learner 'Rev2 B', 10-question 1.3 quiz with worked problems 'some', miss 5 of mixed kinds (2 generated MC, 1 textbook MC, 1 textbook numeric, 1 worked problem)
Also miss 3 in a 2.5 quiz
Open Review mistakes, run a full review session, then use Retry on single entries
checked: Mostly fixed: concepts are now per question, not per section. One correct answer leaves the item at ●○ and closes nothing; a second correct closes only that item; one wrong answer resets only that item (the other six were untouched). BUT for generated questions the concept is still wider than the question: the two missed measurement-level questions (zip codes, °C) collapsed into ONE chip ('missed 2×'), the review asked a third variant (weights in kilograms), and answering that twice marked BOTH original mistakes 'understood' although neither was ever re-asked. In section 2.5 the same keying closes the mistake inside the quiz itself (see new finding mistake-autoclosed-by-sibling). So the round-one symptom — mistakes flipping to 'understood' without being re-asked — survives, narrowed from 'whole section' to 'whole generator'.

steps: With open mistakes, Start review and answer everything correctly twice so all concepts close
Read the page at the end of the session
checked: End state is now consistent: 'Nothing to review. Take a quiz to find gaps.' followed by 'Mistake review: 2 / 2 correct (100%)' and 'Everything you had missed is now understood.' — no leftover 'Concepts to review' list and no dead 'Review mistakes' button. While concepts are still open the summary reads 'N questions still to get right twice in a row' with a 'Keep reviewing' button. The concept chips stay visible above the card for every question of the session (round one lost them from Q3 on).

steps: 10-question 1.3 quiz with worked problems 'mostly'; miss the gum-disease flossing problem, the rainfall problem and the multi-part 'What type of measure scale is being used?'
Open Progress, read the Mistake log
checked: Improved but not gone. [TABLE] markers are now rendered as 'table of N rows' and the multi-part answers read as 'a. ordinal; b. interval; …'. However the gum-disease entry still logs the correct answer as '[PARTS] a. table of 0 rows b. 5.00% c. 93.33% [/PARTS]' — raw [PARTS] markers, plus a wrong row count ('0 rows' for a 5-row table). The same raw [PARTS] block also appears in the quiz's own Model answer box (filed separately as quiz-model-answer-raw-markup).

steps: Take a 1.3 quiz, get a generated relative-frequency table question wrong
Open Progress, Mistake log
checked: Half fixed. The scenario sentence is now included ('Number of days per week that 36 students exercise.'), but the table it refers to is reduced to the placeholder 'table of 5 rows', so the entry still reads '… table of 5 rows · Find the relative frequency for 0 days … your answer: 7.5833 · correct: 0.0833' — the frequencies the answer comes from are still not shown and the logged answer still cannot be checked or learned from.

steps: Choose a learner, open Progress
Click 'switch' in the header
checked: The chooser appears immediately on that click: header shows 'Choose learner', body shows 'Who is learning?', the name box, the Start button and a 'Recent:' list of previous learners. No intermediate 'Choose a learner first.' dead end. Same from the Review page.

steps: On the learner chooser type 'Bartholomew Montgomery-Fitzgerald the Third of Wessex' (53 characters), click Start
checked: Still truncated with no message. The input now carries maxlength=40, so the name is cut mid-word to 'Bartholomew Montgomery-Fitzgerald the Th' and that is what the header, the 'Learning as' card and the Progress heading show. Nothing on the chooser mentions a length limit.

steps: Section 1.1 quiz with worked problems 'only'
Show model answer, click 'I missed it'
checked: The red box now reads 'Not quite.' then 'Model solution:' with the solution and a 'Show me the essentials' button. The empty 'Correct answer:' label is gone (verified in the DOM as well as on screen).

steps: Learner 'Rev2 H sib', section 2.5, 10-question quiz, worked problems 'none' (the quiz contains 8 questions from the desc-mean-median generator)
Answer question 1 ('A sample of 7 ages of club members (years) is: 32; 46; 46; 50; 53; 58; 63. Find the sample mean.') wrong
Answer every later question correctly, including 7 other mean/median questions from the same generator
Read the results page, then open Review mistakes and Progress
expected: The missed question stays open: 'Every question you missed stays open until you answer it correctly twice in a row', so it should appear on the Review page and be asked again
actual: The results page says 'Section 2.5: 9 / 10 correct (90%)' and 'Missed this time: §2.5 — 1 missed', but Review mistakes already says 'Nothing to review. Take a quiz to find gaps.' and the Progress mistake log shows the entry as 'understood' with the section badged 'mastered' — closed by two correct answers on OTHER questions from the same generator, inside the same quiz, without the learner ever seeing the missed question again. The same happens with two misses at once (both closed, review empty).

steps: Learner 'Rev2 I chip', section 2.5, 10-question quiz; miss only the last question, 'A sample of 7 weekly hours worked (hours) is: 14; 21; 22; 23; 24; 25; 39. Find the sample mean.'
Open Review mistakes (one chip, ○○ missed 1×) and click Start review
Answer that question correctly, then Start review again and answer correctly again
Open Progress
expected: The review re-asks the question that was missed (a generated one may come back with fresh numbers, but it should be the same question)
actual: Review question 1 of 1 is 'A sample of 9 prices of lunch (dollars) is: 6; 8; 9; 10; 10; 11; 12; 14; 16. Find the sample median.' and the second pass asks 'A sample of 8 commute times (minutes) … Find the sample mean.' — different data AND a different statistic. The missed question (mean of weekly hours) is never asked, yet after those two answers it is marked 'understood'. Same in §1.3: two separate missed measurement-level questions (zip codes; temperatures in °C) collapse into ONE chip 'missed 2×', so Progress lists 8 mistakes while Review shows 7 chips, the review asks a third variant ('weights of packages in kilograms', later 'survey responses poor/fair/good/excellent'), and closing it marks both originals understood.

steps: Have one open mistake on a generated question (e.g. §2.5 'A sample of 7 weekly hours worked … Find the sample mean.')
Open Review mistakes and read the chip, then click Start review and read the question
Separately, miss both De Anza questions 'The average number of distance learning credit units …' (A17 and B7) in a 1.3 quiz and look at the chip list
expected: The chip labels identify the questions the review will ask, and two different questions are distinguishable in the list
actual: The chip shows the stem of the missed question ('§2.5 A sample of 7 weekly hours worked (hours) is: 14; 21; 22; 2… ○○ missed 1×') but the review asks a different variant, so the label never matches what is on screen. Chips are also truncated at ~55 characters, so two genuinely different questions can produce two identical-looking chips ('§1.3 The average number of distance learning credit units for al… ○○ missed 1×' twice) with no way to tell them apart.

steps: Load a learner saved by the earlier build: profile with review entries keyed by section ({'3.1': {conceptTag:'3.1', streak:0, required:2, status:'open', misses:2}, same for 3.2 and 3.3}) and six mistakes tagged with their sectionId (learner 'QA Legacy One')
Open Review mistakes: three chips, §3.1/§3.2/§3.3, ○○ missed 2×
Start review and answer all three questions correctly; repeat twice more (9 correct answers in all)
Then Retry a single legacy mistake from Progress and answer it correctly, twice
expected: An older learner's mistakes can still be worked off: the review asks the questions they missed and the streak advances until the entries close
actual: The learner loads fine (header, progress table, mistake log all intact) but the old entries can never be cleared. Every review session asks RANDOM questions from the section rather than the ones the learner missed ('Find P(R).', 'Write the symbols for the probability that a student…', a fresh prob-or-rule), and no answer ever counts: after three full passes plus two correct Retries the chips are still '○○ missed 2×', the stored review entries are byte-for-byte unchanged (streak 0, status open, lastAt still the old date), and all six mistakes still read 'still open' in Progress. Retry does open the right question, but its result is not recorded either.

steps: Learner 'Rev2 D', section 1.2, 5-question quiz; answer questions 1 and 2 (both wrong)
Open a second tab on the same quiz URL (context.newPage())
In tab 2 answer all 5 questions correctly to the end
Go back to tab 1 and answer its remaining 3 questions (wrong), then open Progress in each tab
expected: The second tab either resumes the same attempt or says the quiz is open elsewhere; one 5-question quiz counts as 5 answers
actual: Tab 2 silently restarts the same quiz at 'Question 1 of 5' with the same questions and empty controls (sessionStorage is per tab, so tab 1's progress is invisible there). Both tabs are then recorded: tab 2 finishes '5 / 5 correct (100%)', tab 1 finishes '0 / 5 correct (0%)', and Progress ends up with ANSWERED 10 / CORRECT 50% for a single 5-question quiz, plus 5 mistake-log entries for questions that were answered correctly in the other tab. The two tabs also disagree until reload (tab 2 shows 1.2 as 7 answered / 71% / mastered-looking, tab 1 shows 10 answered / 50%).

steps: Learner 'Rev2 C', chapter 3, 15-question chapter quiz
Miss 2 questions in §3.1 and 2 in §3.3, answer the rest correctly (final score 11/15 = 73%)
Open Progress and read the Sections table
expected: 'LAST QUIZ' for a section reflects how the learner did on that section's questions
actual: Every one of the five section rows shows LAST QUIZ 73% — the whole-chapter score — even where the section column next to it says 33% (3.1: ANSWERED 3, CORRECT 33%, LAST QUIZ 73%; same for 3.3). A learner reading the row cannot tell which sections went badly from the LAST QUIZ column.

steps: Section 1.3 quiz with worked problems 'mostly'
Reach the gum-disease flossing problem ('Sixty adults with gum disease…') and click 'Show model answer'
expected: The model answer is rendered like the question: a real table and lettered parts
actual: The box shows raw markup — '[PARTS]', then 'a.' followed by the whole table flattened into one tab-separated run ('# Flossing per Week\tFrequency\t… 0\t27\t0.4500\t0.4500 1\t18\t0.3000\t0.7500 …'), then 'b. 5.00%', 'c. 93.33%', then '[/PARTS]'. The learner is asked to self-mark 'I got it / I missed it' against that.

steps: Open section 1.4 (the page says '10 questions ready · 0 checked instantly · 10 worked problems with model answers')
Set worked problems to 'none', click Start quiz
expected: Either the 'none' option is not offered for a section that has only worked problems, or the page explains and offers a way back
actual: The page is a dead end: the body is the single lower-case line 'no questions available for this scope' with no buttons and no link back; only the header nav gets the learner out. Hit while setting up the two-tab test, so reported as something I had to work around.

steps: Section 3.2 quizzes, worked problems 'none'
Look at the generated independence-check questions (prob-independent-check)
expected: A probability in the premise is between 0 and 1
actual: The generator produces impossible premises, e.g. 'P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.1, and P(A AND B) = -0.01. True or false: A and B are independent events.' (seen twice, also 'P(A AND B) = -0.015'). The question is still gradeable, but the premise cannot happen. Noting only — content is audited separately.
